title: Idempotency header rewrite during edge redirect causes lost billing debits
creator: Marco Chen
description: Summary: We observed a class of incidents where client requests that were transparently redirected at the edge (region/route aliasing, HTTP 307 style path remap) had their idempotency token rewritten by the edge proxy. That rewrite prevents the downstream billing subsystem from matching the in-flight debit record, which in some timing windows results in the usage debit never being recorded. Symptoms: small but measurable underbilling for a subset of multi-step streaming and retrying clients, and transient divergence between real requests seen by the runtime and billing ledger counts. Impact: medium to high for affected orgs (loss of recorded usage; customers may not be charged correctly and accounting shards need reconciliation).
repro_steps: 1) Use a test client that sets an Idempotency-Key header and retries on 3xx redirects.
2) Configure the edge to remap the request (route aliasing) and issue a 307 redirect to a secondary route.
3) Observe that the edge proxy rewrites the Idempotency-Key on redirect (hash-prefix applied).
4) Downstream billing path creates a transient pending debit using the client-supplied idempotency token.
5) When the request completes, the final commit uses the rewritten token, causing the ledger commit lookup to miss the pending debit and drop the accounting entry.
6) Reproduce under higher concurrency and with streaming partial-acks to increase race probability.
logs_snippets: edge: INFO 2026-03-01T14:12:04Z Received request id=abc123 idempotency=key-xyz
edge: DEBUG 2026-03-01T14:12:04Z Redirecting to /r2 with idempotency=rewrote:key-abc
billing: WARN 2026-03-01T14:12:04Z PendingDebit created idempotency=key-xyz pending_id=pend-594
billing: ERROR 2026-03-01T14:12:04Z Commit lookup miss for idempotency=rewrite:key-abc; pending debit pend-594 not found for commit, dropping write
investigation_notes: Edge proxy applies a deterministic prefix rewrite for idempotency keys when crossing route boundaries. This was added to avoid collisions across org-scoped caches but wasn't coordinated with billing semantics.
Billing ledger uses the raw idempotency token as the key for matching pending->commit flows. When the token is mutated mid-flight, the commit path fails to locate the pending entry.
Race window is larger when streaming responses cause the commit path to run on a different worker than the pending creation (intra-host handoff).
Observed similar patterns in replay tests, but rate was low; production SRE telemetry highlights a handful of orgs with consistent negative reconciliation deltas over the last 30 days.
proposed_fix: Short-term mitigation: update edge to preserve Idempotency-Key verbatim for any request that will be metered/billed (config flag per-route). Roll out to affected regions only.

Long-term: change billing matching to use an immutable debit identifier returned by the metering precommit step instead of relying on client-supplied idempotency tokens. This will require plumbing a debit_id through redirects and retries (explicit header or attach to the routing context).

Backfill plan: run a reconciliation job that searches for pending debits in the window and attaches commits where request logs show a final commit without an associated pending record. For safety, mark any inferred backfills and require manual approval above threshold.

Add invariant tests: e2e test that exercises redirect + retry + streaming to ensure pending->commit linkage survives remap; unit test for rewrite path to assert idempotency header passthrough when meterable=true.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No more rewrite of Idempotency-Key for meterable routes by default; configuration present and documented.
2) Billing subsystem accepts either client idempotency token or debit_id header; pending->commit matching succeeds in redirected scenarios in automated e2e tests.
3) Reconciliation job can detect and rectify missed debits; in a canary run on a single org it should recover >=95% of missed entries without false positives.
4) Instrumentation added: metric meter.pending_miss_count with per-route and per-org tagging; alerts for >10 misses/hour per org.
notes_to_QA: Create a test harness that runs redirects under configurable latency to reproduce the race window.
Verify that streaming partial-acks and chunked responses do not affect matching when debit_id is used.
Test canary rollouts: enable idempotency passthrough in one region first and monitor pending_miss_count and reconciliation offsets.
comments: 2026-03-02 Marco Chen: Initial report from SRE; attached reconciliation diffs for orgs 309 and 441. Asking ENG to triage and propose mitigation.

2026-03-03 Lena Ortega: Confirmed repro locally with proxy shim that rewrites header. Observed pending debit created with original token and commit attempted with rewritten token. Starting patch to short-circuit rewrite for meterable routes.
2026-03-05 Aaron Diaz (SRE): Added dashboards to track per-route pending_miss_count and reconciliation backlog. Will throttle reconciliation to avoid DB pressure.

2026-03-08 Marco Chen: Design note: plan to introduce debit_id token - we need cross-team review from runtime and edge to agree header name and TTL semantics. Scheduling design review Tues 2026-03-09.
2026-03-09 Lena Ortega: Submitted PR to edge to opt-out idempotency rewrite when X-Redwood-Meterable=true. Unit tests included. Need codeowner review from runtime-team and billing-team.
